title: Only questions
rule: Every caption and balloon is a question; even the answer and the thanks are offered as questions.
declares: answer and thanks recast as questions (same content, same speakers)
made: HANDMADE black cut-paper shadow puppets (the b1m2 figure model: agent in profile with waistcoat, sleeve garter, spectacles and pencil cut through; the stranger as a bust with cloche hat) with their control rods: thin sticks from the chest and the working hand down past the bottom of each screen
eight warm, lantern-lit paper screens (amber hotspot to a red-brown rim over the fibre of the LoC 1934 sheet), distinct from page 05's grey slat light

cut set pieces: desk and lamp, ticket window with TICKET OFFICE in light through the header, clock at 4:10 with pendulum, cupboard (closed in P6, opened in P7-P8 on its left jamb), SERVICE door with its card
the ANRC 1922 key cutout (99-ways-template piece) used as a black shadow shape on a cut hook, with a paper SERVICE tag
the memo is a blank paper card on the desk (its words are carried by the P1 question, so no sentence on the page is a statement)
all captions and balloons in the shared pen hand: 13 texts, every sentence a question; folio by pen99.folio

substitutions.answer: Ten past four, by the clock?
substitutions.memo: not lettered on the card; P1 asks: 'Doesn't his memo say 4:15, open the SERVICE door, and isn't the key in the cupboard?'

lines.question: Pardon me — have you the right time?
lines.answer: Ten past four, by the clock?
lines.forgetting: Well, here I am... and what for?

texts: Doesn't his memo say 4:15, open the SERVICE door, and isn't the key in the cupboard?
So up he gets, and off he goes for the key, doesn't he?
Pardon me — have you the right time?
And who's that at the ticket window?
Ten past four, by the clock?
And where would he look, if not up at the clock?
And what's behind the cupboard door?
Isn't that the brass key, on its hook, tagged SERVICE, in plain view?
Well, here I am... and what for?
And the key, still on its hook?
And the SERVICE door, still closed?

events.E0: P1 at the desk with the memo card (asked in the caption); P2 he walks toward the closed cupboard
events.E1: P3 the stranger soft behind the TICKET OFFICE glass; question balloon
events.E2: P4 he looks up at the clock (4:10); answer as a question
events.E3: P5 she turns away behind the glass; thanks as a question
events.E4: P6 his hand on the knob of the closed cupboard ('what's behind the cupboard door?'); P7 the cupboard open, the key on its hook, tag SERVICE
events.E5: P8 pencil to his chin, the forgetting line; the key still on its hook, the SERVICE door closed (both asked in slips)

beat: the P7 cupboard leaf swings open on the screen (0, 35, 70, 112 degrees) and the key's shadow comes into the light; then the forgetting balloon is laid in P8
beat_frames: b01: P7 cupboard closed, P8 without balloon
b04: leaf open, key on its hook

self_check.check: Every sentence on the page ends with a question mark. -> measured on the page's text list (13 texts, 13 sentences, all ending '?'); signs and folio are labels, not sentences
self_check.evidence: measured (sentence check, size) and perceptually judged (from frames) by the maker; independent readers not yet run

weaknesses: 'Much obliged?' reads oddly by design; a reader may take it as sarcasm rather than thanks
the memo card is blank: the memo's content lives only in the P1 question
the stranger is a soft brown shadow behind the glass; her hat and coat read, her face does not
P7 is a close-up without the agent, so E4 is split across P6 (hand on knob) and P7 (open cupboard)
